segments.arabic:
١١١١٢- خنساء بنت عمرو
بن الشّريد «١» بن ثعلبة بن عصية بن خفاف بن امرئ القيس بن بهثة بن سليم السلمية الشاعرة المشهورة، اسمها تماضر، بمثناة فوقانية أوله وضاد معجمة- وفي ذلك يقول دريد بن الصمة حين رآها تهنأ إبلا لها ثم تجردت واغتسلت فأعجبته فخطبها، فأبت فقال فيها:
حيّوا تماضر واربعوا صحبي ... وقفوا فإنّ وقوفكم حسبي
ما إن رأيت ولا سمعت به ... كاليوم طالي أينق جرب
مبتذّلا تبدو محاسنه ... يضع الهناء مواضع النّقب
أخناس قد هام الفؤاد بكم ... واعتاده داء من الحبّ «٢»
[الكامل]
(١) أسد الغابة ت ٦٨٨٣، الاستيعاب ت ٣٣٦٣.
(٢) ينظر البيت الأول في ديوان دريد بن الصمة وهو في ديوانه ص ٤٣. وبعده:
أخناس قد هام الفؤادكم ... وأصابه تبل من الحبّ
ومناسبة هذه الأبيات كما قال صاحب الأغاني ١٠/ ٢١، ٢٢، مرّ دريد ابن الصمة بالخنساء بنت عمرو ابن الشريد وهي تهنأ بعيرا لها، وقد تبذلت حتى فرغت منه، ثمّ نضّت عنها ثيابها فاغتسلت ودريد بن الصمة يراها وهي لا تشعر به فأعجبته، فانصرف إلى رحلها وأنشأ يقول ... ويروى البيت الأول في الوحشيات: ٢٥: «حيّوا أمامة وانظروا» والّذي عليه جميع المصادر (تماضر) وهو ما يتناسب. أربعوا: الإرباع الاطمئنان والإقامة في المكان. وينظر الأعلام ٢/ ٣٩٩.
segments.english:
11112—Khansa bint 'Amr

ibn al-Sharid (1) ibn Tha'laba ibn 'Usayya ibn Khifaf ibn Imru' al-Qays ibn Bahtha ibn Sulaym, the Sulami woman and famous poet. Her name was Tumadir—with an initial ta bearing two dots above and a dotted dad. In connection with this, Duraid ibn al-Simma saw her applying ointment to some camels of hers, after which she stripped and bathed. He was taken with her and proposed marriage to her, but she refused, so he said of her:

Greet Tumadir, and stay awhile, my companions;
stop, for your stopping is enough for me.

Never have I seen or heard tell of anyone
like one daubing mangy she-camels today—

dressed for work, with beauty showing,
placing ointment wherever the sores lie.

O Khunas, the heart has become enamored of you,
and a sickness born of love has beset it. (2)

[al-Kamil meter]

(1) Usd al-Ghaba, entry 6883; al-Isti'ab, entry 3363.

(2) See the first verse in the Diwan of Duraid ibn al-Simma; it is in his Diwan, p. 43. It is followed by:

O Khunas, the heart has become enamored [of you],
and wasting love-sickness has afflicted it.

The occasion of these verses, as the author of al-Aghani, 10/21–22, states, was that Duraid ibn al-Simma passed by Khansa bint 'Amr ibn al-Sharid while she was applying ointment to a camel of hers. She was dressed for work until she had finished with it; then she took off her clothes and bathed. Duraid ibn al-Simma was watching her without her being aware of him. He admired her, went to her camp, and began to recite… The first verse is also transmitted in al-Wahshiyyat, p. 25, as: “Greet Umama and look.” The reading found in all the sources is “Tumadir,” and that is the reading that fits. “Stay awhile” (arbi'u): al-irba' means settling at ease and remaining in a place. See also al-A'lam, 2/399.

segments.arabic:
فبلغتها خطبته، فقالت: لا أدع بني عمي الطوال مثل عوالي الرماح، وأتزوّج شيخا، فلما بلغه ذلك قال من أبيات:
وقاك اللَّه يا ابنة آل عمرو ... من الفتيان أمثالي ونفسي
وقالت إنّه شيخ كبير ... وهل خبّرتها أنّي ابن أمس
[وقد علم المراضع في جمادى ... إذا استعجلن عن حزّ بنهس]
[الوافر] إلى أن قال:
وأنّي لا أبيت بغير نحر ... وأبدأ بالأرامل حين أمسى
وأنّي لا يهرّ الكلب ضيفي ... ولا جاري يبيت خبيث نفس
فأجابته بأبيات.
قال أبو عمر: قدمت على النبي ﷺ مع قومها من بني سليم، فأسلمت معهم، فذكروا أنّ رسول اللَّه ﷺ كان يستنشدها ويعجبه شعرها، وكانت تنشده، وهو يقول: «هيه يا خناس»، ويومئ بيده.
قالوا: وكانت الخنساء تقول في أول أمرها البيتين أو الثلاثة حتى قتل أخوها شقيقها معاوية بن عمرو، وقتل أخوها لأبيها صخر، وكان أحبهما إليها، لأنه كان حليما جوادا محبوبا في العشيرة، كان غزا بني أسد فطعنه أبو ثور الأسدي طعنة مرض منها حولا، ثم مات، فلما قتل أخواها أكثرت من الشعر، فمن قولها في صخر:
أعينيّ جودا ولا تجمدا ... ألا تبكيان لصخر النّدى
ألا تبكيان الجريء الجميل ... ألّا تبكيان الفتى السّيّدا
طويل النّجاد عظيم الرّماد ... ساد عشيرته أمردا «١»
[المتقارب] ومن قولها فيه:
وإنّ صخرا لمولانا وسيّدنا ... وإنّ صخرا إذا نشتو لنحّار
(١) البيت للخنساء ترثي أخاها صخرا كما في ديوانها ص ٣٥ وبعده:
ألا تبكيان الجريء الجميل ... ألا تبكيان الفتى السّيّدا
طويل النّجاد رفيع العماد ... ساد عشيرته أمردا
تنظر الأبيات في أسد الغابة ترجمة رقم (٦٨٨٣)، والاستيعاب ترجمة رقم (٣٣٦٣) .
segments.english:
His proposal reached her, and she said, “I will not leave my tall paternal cousins, who are like the upper shafts of spears, and marry an old man.” When this reached him, he said, in some verses:

May Allah protect you, O daughter of the house of Amr,
from young men like me—and from me myself!

She said, “He is an aged shaykh”;
but did you tell her that I am a son of yesterday?

[The nursing women knew, in Jumada,
when, in their haste, they gnawed flesh from the bone rather than cut it.]

[al-Wafir]

He continued until he said:

I never pass a night without slaughtering,
and when evening comes, the widows come first.

My dog does not growl at my guest,
nor does my neighbor pass the night with a troubled heart.

She answered him with verses.

Abu Umar said: She came to the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—with her people from Banu Sulaym, and she embraced Islam together with them. They related that the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—would ask her to recite poetry to him, and that her poetry pleased him. She would recite to him while he said, “Go on, O Khunas,” and gestured with his hand.

They said: At first, al-Khansa would compose only two or three verses. Then her full brother, Muawiya ibn Amr, was killed, and her paternal half-brother Sakhr was killed. Sakhr was the one she loved more, because he was forbearing, generous, and beloved within the clan. He had raided Banu Asad, and Abu Thawr al-Asadi dealt him a thrust that left him ill for a year; then he died. When her two brothers were killed, she composed poetry abundantly. Among what she said about Sakhr was:

O my two eyes, pour forth and do not dry up!
Will you not weep for Sakhr, the man of generosity?

Will you not weep for the bold and handsome one?
Will you not weep for the lordly young man?

Long of sword-belt, great of ashes,
he became lord of his clan while still beardless.¹

[al-Mutaqarib]

Among what she said about him was:

Indeed, Sakhr is surely our patron and our chief;
and indeed, when winter comes, Sakhr is a great slaughterer of camels.

¹ The verse is by al-Khansa, lamenting her brother Sakhr, as in her Diwan, p. 35. It is followed by:

Will you not weep for the bold and handsome one?
Will you not weep for the lordly young man?

Long of sword-belt, lofty of pillar,
he became lord of his clan while still beardless.

The verses may be consulted in Usd al-Ghaba, biography no. 6883, and al-Isti'ab, biography no. 3363.

segments.arabic:
أشمّ أبلج يأتمّ الهداة به ... كأنّه علم في رأسه نار «١»
[البسيط] قال: وأجمع أهل العلم بالشعر أنه لم تكن امرأة قبلها ولا بعدها أشعر منها.
وذكر الزّبير بن بكّار، عن محمد بن الحسن المخزومي، وهو المعروف بابن زبالة، أحد المتروكين، عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد اللَّه، عن أبيه، عن أبي وجزة، عن أبيه، قال:
حضرت الخنساء بنت عمرو السلمية حرب القادسية ومعها بنوها أربعة رجال، فذكر موعظتها لهم وتحريضهم على القتال، وعدم الفرار، وفيها: إنكم أسلمتم طائعين، وهاجرتم مختارين، وإنكم لبنو أب واحد وأم واحدة، ما هجنت آباءكم، ولا فضحت أخوالكم، فلما أصبحوا باشروا القتال واحدا بعد واحد حتى قتلوا، وكل منهم أنشد قبل أن يستشهد رجزا، فأنشد الأول:
يا إخوتي إنّ العجوز النّاصحه ... قد نصحتنا إذ دعتنا البارحه
بمقالة ذات بيان واضحه ... وإنّما تلقون عند الصّائحه
من آل ساسان كلابا نابحة
[الرجز] وأنشد الثاني:
إنّ العجوز ذات حزم وجلد ... قد أمرتنا بالسداد والرّشد
نصيحة منها وبرّا بالولد ... فباكروا الحرب حماة في العدد
[الرجز] وأنشد الثالث:
واللَّه لا نعصي العجوز حرفا ... نصحا وبرّا صادقا ولطفا
فبادروا الحرب الضّروس زحفا ... حتّى تلفّوا آل كسرى لفّا
[الرجز] وأنشد الرابع:
لست لخنساء ولا للأخرم ... ولا لعمرو ذي السّناء الأقدم
(١) البيت للخنساء وهو في ديوانها ص ٤٠ وبعده:
وإنّ صخرا لمقدام إذا ركبوا ... وإن صخرا إذا جاعوا لعقّار
segments.english:
High-nosed and bright-browed, whom the guides follow as their leader—
As though he were a mountain with a fire upon its summit.¹

[al-Basit meter]

He said: The scholars of poetry unanimously agreed that there was no woman, either before or after her, who was a greater poet than she.

al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar related, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Makhzumi—known as Ibn Zabala, one of the abandoned transmitters—on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah, from his father, from Abu Wajza, from his father, who said:

al-Khansa bint Amr al-Sulamiyya attended the Battle of al-Qadisiyya, and with her were her sons, four men. He then related her admonition to them and her urging them to fight and not to flee. It included: “You embraced Islam willingly and emigrated by choice. You are indeed the sons of one father and one mother. I did not dishonor your fathers, nor did I bring disgrace upon your maternal uncles.” When morning came, they engaged in the fighting one after another until they were killed. Each of them recited rajaz verse before being martyred. The first recited:

O my brothers, the sincere old counselor
Counseled us when she summoned us last night,
With words whose meaning was lucid and clear.
At the battle cry, you will encounter only
Barking dogs from the House of Sasan.

[al-Rajaz meter]

The second recited:

The old woman, possessed of resolve and endurance,
Has commanded us to pursue the sound and righteous course,
As counsel from her and kindness toward her children.
So meet the war at daybreak, defenders amid the host.

[al-Rajaz meter]

The third recited:

By Allah, we shall not disobey the old woman in a single word;
Her counsel was sincere and true, given with devotion and kindness.
So advance at once upon the grinding war in marching ranks,
Until you envelop the House of Kisra completely.

[al-Rajaz meter]

The fourth recited:

I am no son of al-Khansa, nor of al-Akhram,
Nor of Amr, possessor of glory from ancient times—

¹ The verse is by al-Khansa and appears in her Diwan, p. 40. It is followed by:

Indeed, Sakhr was one who boldly advanced when they mounted,
And indeed, when they went hungry, Sakhr would slaughter camels.

segments.arabic:
إن لم أرد في الجيش جيش الأعجم ... ماض على الهول خضمّ حضرمي «١» .
[الرجز] وكل من الأسانيد أطول من هذا، قال: فبلغها الخبر، فقالت: الحمد للَّه الّذي شرفني بقتلهم، وأرجو من ربي أن يجمعني بهم في مستقرّ رحمته.
قالوا: وكان عمر بن الخطاب يعطي الخنساء أرزاق أولادها الأربعة حتى قبض.
قلت: ومن شعرها في أخيها:
ألا يا صخر لا أنساك حتّى ... أفارق مهجتي ويشقّ رمسي
يذكّرني طلوع الشّمس صخرا ... وأبكيه لكلّ غروب شمس
ولولا كثرة الباكين حولي ... على إخوانهم لقتلت نفسي
[الوافر] ومن شعرها فيه:
ألا يا صخر إن أبكيت عيني ... فقد أضحكتني دهرا طويلا
ذكرتك في نساء معولات ... وكنت أحقّ من أبدى العويلا
دفعت بك الجليل وأنت حيّ ... ومن ذا يدفع الخطب الجليلا
إذا قبح البكاء على قتيل ... رأيت بكاءك الحسن الجميلا «٢»
[الوافر] ويقال إنها دخلت على عائشة وعليها صدار من شعر، فقالت لها: يا خنساء، هذا نهي رسول اللَّه ﷺ عنه، فقالت: ما علمت، ولكن هذا له قصة، زوّجني أبي رجلا مبذّرا فأذهب ماله، فأتيت إلى صخر فقسم ماله شطرين، فأعطاني شطرا خيارا، ثم فعل زوجي ذلك مرة أخرى، فقسم أخي ماله شطرين فأعطاني خبرهما، فقالت له امرأته: أما ترضي أن تعطيها النصف حتى تعطيها الخيار، فقال:
واللَّه لا أمنحها شرارها ... وهي الّتي أرحض عني عارها
ولو هلكت خرّقت خمارها ... واتّخذت من شعر صدارها
[الرجز]
(١) تنظر الأبيات في الاستيعاب ترجمة رقم (٣٣٦٣) .
(٢) تنظر الأبيات في الديوان ص ٨٢، وهذا الشعر قالته الخنساء تبكي أخاها معاوية لمّا قتله بنو مرّة، وزعم أبو عبيدة أنها قالت هذا الشعر في أخيها صخر لما دفن بأرض بني سليم عند جبل عسيب وهو من غرر مراثيها.
segments.english:
If I do not advance with the army against the army of the non-Arabs—
pressing on in the face of terror, a noble, bountiful Hadrami.¹
[Rajaz]

Every one of the chains of transmission is longer than this. He said: When the news reached her, she said, “Praise be to Allah, who has honored me through their being slain. I hope that my Lord will unite me with them in the abode of His mercy.”

They said: Umar ibn al-Khattab continued to give al-Khansa the stipends of her four sons until he died.

I say: Among her poetry about her brother is:

O Sakhr, I shall not forget you until
my soul and I part and my grave is cleft open.

The rising sun reminds me of Sakhr,
and at every sunset I weep for him.

Were it not for the multitude of weepers around me,
mourning their brothers, I would have killed myself.
[Wafir]

Among her poetry about him is:

O Sakhr, though you have made my eye weep,
you made me laugh for a long age.

I remembered you among wailing women,
and I had the greatest right of any to voice the wail.

Through you I repelled grave calamity while you were alive;
and who can repel the grave catastrophe?

Though weeping over a slain man be deemed ugly,
I regard weeping for you as fair and beautiful.²
[Wafir]

It is said that she entered upon Aisha wearing a bodice made of hair. Aisha said to her, “O al-Khansa, the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—forbade this.” She replied, “I did not know, but there is a story behind it. My father married me to a spendthrift man, and he squandered his wealth. I went to Sakhr, and he divided his wealth into two halves and gave me the choicer half. Then my husband did the same thing once again, so my brother divided his wealth into two halves and gave me the better of the two.” His wife said to him, “Are you not content with giving her half, that you must also give her the choicer portion?” He said:

By Allah, I will not give her its worst,
for she is the one whose shame I wash away from me.

If I should perish, she would rend her veil
and make herself a bodice of hair.
[Rajaz]

[Textual note: The printed Arabic has khabarahuma, “their report”; the context and the Urdu witness support khayrahuma, “the better of the two.”]

(1) See the verses in al-Isti'ab, entry no. 3363.

(2) See the verses in the Diwan, p. 82. al-Khansa composed this poem while mourning her brother Muawiya when Banu Murra killed him. Abu Ubayda claimed that she composed it about her brother Sakhr when he was buried in the territory of Banu Sulaym, near Mount 'Asib. It is one of the choicest of her elegies.

unresolved.arabic_span: أخناس قد هام الفؤادكم ... وأصابه تبل من الحبّ
unresolved.explanation: The printed الفؤادكم is grammatically defective and is probably missing the preposition ب, as in the parallel main-text verse الفؤاد بكم. None of the supplied witnesses contains the cited Diwan line, so the emendation cannot be independently verified. The translation therefore marks “[of you]” as supplied.

The masculine participle مبتذلا most naturally attaches to the preceding طالي, while the narrative identifies Khansa as the person described. The supplied witness paraphrases the scene but omits the verse. The gender-neutral translation preserves the sense without deciding the precise grammatical attachment.

The canonical printed word خبرهما literally means “their report” and is incoherent here. The context, Urdu witness, and a parallel al-Isabah text support خيرهما, “the better of the two,” which the translation adopts transparently; the precise origin of the printed reading cannot be established from the supplied evidence.
